43WC: The Eternal Being is one, and he is met by the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God, By the True Guru's grace, is He obtained.
B2R1: The Saloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur ji.
CVCZ: Gun gobind = the qualities of Gobind. Akarath = in vain. Keen = he has made.
If you have never sung the qualities of the Lord, then you have made your human birth worthless.
If you do not sing the Praises of the Lord, your life is rendered useless.
If you have not sung the praises of the World-Lord, you have wasted your life in vain.
O mind! The one who has not sung the qualities of Gobind, he has made this human birth worthless.
5P84: Kahu = say. Mana = O mind! Jih bidh = in what manner, in the way that. Jal kau = to the water. Meen = the fish ||1||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on doing the Lord's devotion (and make him the support of your life in the way) that the fish (keeps the water as the support of its own life). ||1||
Says Nanak, meditate, vibrate upon the Lord; immerse your mind in Him, like the fish in the water. ||1||
Says Nanak, meditate you on God, O man, like the way, the fish loves water.
Sri Guru ji says: therefore do the devotion of Hari in the way that the fish serves the water. ||1||
8G8U: Bikhian siau = with the objects of the senses. Kahe = why? Nimakh = (निमेष) for as long as the blink of an eye. Na hohi = you do not become. Udas = turned away.
Why do you remain (so) absorbed in the objects of the senses? Not even for as long as the blink of an eye do you turn your mind away from them.
Why are you engrossed in sin and corruption? You are not detached, even for a moment!
Why are you engrossed in the deadly sins and becomes not detached even for a moment?
O mind! Why are you (rachio) making love with the objects of the senses, and do not become detached from those objects even for the space of a blink?
PSYM: Parai na = it does not fall. Phas = the noose ||2||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on doing the Lord's devotion. (By the grace of devotion) the noose of the messengers of death does not fall (around the neck). ||2||
Says Nanak, meditate, vibrate upon the Lord, and you shall not be caught in the noose of death. ||2||
Say Nanak, contemplate you your God, O man, that death's noose may fall on you not.
Sri Guru ji says: even now do the devotion of Hari, so that the noose of Yama will not fall around your neck. ||2||
HCV5: Tarnapo = youth (तरुण = young). Iau hi = just like that, in heedlessness. Jara = old age. Jeet leeo = it has conquered.
(Your) youth has passed away in heedlessness alone; (now) old age has conquered your body.
Your youth has passed away like this, and old age has overtaken your body.
They youth has passed away in vain and old age has overcome your body.
O mind! The time of (tarnapo) the state of youth went by just so, uselessly, among the objects of the senses, and now old age has conquered all the senses.
6GPB: Audh = the life-span. Jat hai beet = it is going by ||3||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on doing the Lord's devotion. The life-span is passing away. ||3||
Says Nanak, meditate, vibrate upon the Lord; your life is fleeting away! ||3||
Says Nanak, dwell you on your God, O man, your life is fleeting away.
Sri Guru ji says: now this span of old age too is passing by, therefore do the devotion of Hari. ||3||
X6MU: Biradh = old. Soojhai nahi = it is not understood. Kal = death. Aan = having come.
(Look, you have now) become old (but even now you) do not understand that death has come (upon your head).
You have become old, and you do not understand that death is overtaking you.
You have become old and you see not that death has overtaken you.
O foolish man, you have become old, and with your eyes too you cannot see; death also has come near.
66AX: Nar bavre = O mad man! Na bhajah = you do not repeat ||4||
Nanak says — O mad man! Why do you not do the devotion of the Lord? ||4||
Says Nanak, you are insane! Why do you not remember and meditate on God? ||4||
Says Nanak, O crazy man, why remember you not your Illustrious Lord?
Sri Guru ji says: why do you not do the devotion of Bhagvan? The meaning being, even now do the devotion.
1GQF: Dara = the wife. Sampat sagal = all the property, the whole estate. Jin man = do not consider, do not hold. Apuni kar = taking it as your own.
(O brother!) Wealth, wife, the whole estate — do not hold (them) as your own.
Your wealth, spouse, and all the possessions which you claim as your own
Wealth, wife and all other property, which you deem your own;
Wealth and wife and property such as horses and elephants — do not (man) consider these as your own.
QEL8: In mah = out of all these. Sangi = a companion. Sachi jan = know (this matter) for certain ||5||
O Nanak! Know this matter for truth, that out of all of these not even one can become your companion. ||5||
- none of these shall go along with you in the end. O Nanak, know this as true. ||5||
None of these shall be your companion. Know you this as true, O Nanak.
Among these not one is your (sangi) companion who will go with you. Sri Guru ji says: understand this teaching of mine as true. ||5||
2BH7: Patit = those fallen into vices. Patit udharan = the saviour of the fallen from their vices. Bhai = (plural of the word 'bhau'). Bhai haran = the remover of all fears. Anath ke nath = the master of the masterless.
The Lord is the saviour of the vice-ridden from their vices, the remover of all fears, and the master of the masterless.
He is the Saving Grace of sinners, the Destroyer of fear, the Master of the masterless.
God is the Saviour of sinners, the Destroyer of fear and the Master of the masterless.
Hari is the redeemer of the fallen, the remover of every kind of fear, the master of the masterless.
C042: Tih = him (the Lord). Janeeai = one ought to know (that). Sath = with ||6||
Nanak says — one ought to understand that Lord in this way, that he dwells with you for ever. ||6||
Says Nanak, realize and know Him, who is always with you. ||6||
Says Nanak, realise you Him, who abides ever with you.
He dwells with you for all time; Sri Guru ji says: him one ought to (janeeai) know.
BDU3: Jih = the one (the Lord) who. To kau = to you. Tan siau = with him (the Lord). Nehu = love.
The Lord who gave you a body and gave you wealth — with him you formed no love,
He has given you your body and wealth, but you are not in love with Him.
You enshrine not affection for Him, for has given you human body and riches.
O mad man! The one who gave you body, mind and wealth — with him you have formed no affection.
M3YB: Nar bavre = O mad man! Deen = distressed ||7||
Nanak says — O mad man! Why do you now wander about distressed and dismayed? (The meaning being, without remembering that Lord, dismay was bound to come.) ||7||
Says Nanak, you are insane! Why do you now shake and tremble so helplessly? ||7||
Says Nanak, O crazy man, why now wobble you like an abject person?

695N: Sampai = wealth. Ar = and. Jih = the one who. Neeke = fine, beautiful. Dham = houses.
The Lord who gave you a body, gave you wealth, gave you property, gave you comforts and gave you fine houses,
He has given you your body, wealth, property, peace and beautiful mansions.
He, who has blessed you with body, wealth, property happiness and beauteous mansions.
O mind! That Ram who gave you (tan) a body and wealth and property and every kind of comfort,
25VM: Nanak says — O mind! Listen, why do you not remember that Lord? ||8||
Says Nanak, listen, mind: why don't you remember the Lord in meditation? ||8||
Says Nanak, hear you, O my soul, why contemplate not you your Lord?
Sri Guru ji says: why do you not remember that Ram? ||8||
DX06: The Lord alone is the giver of all comforts; there is no other (equal to him).
The Lord is the Giver of all peace and comfort. There is no other at all.
The Lord is the Giver of all comforts. Without there is not another.
O mind, listen! The giver of all comforts is the one Ram alone; there is no other.
ZSH9: Tih = him (Ram). Simrat = while remembering. A high spiritual state ||9||
Nanak says — O mind! Listen, by remembering (his Name) the high spiritual state (too) is obtained. ||9||
Says Nanak, listen, mind: meditating in remembrance on Him, salvation is attained. ||9||

3DMV: Paeeai = one obtains. Tai = you. Re meet = O friend!
O friend! Go on doing the devotion of that Lord, by remembering whose Name the high spiritual state is obtained.
Remembering Him in meditation, salvation is attained; vibrate and meditate on Him, O my friend.
Remember you Him, O my friend, by contemplating whom one is emancipated.
O friend, mind, listen! The one by whose remembrance the high state comes about — do the remembrance of the Name of that Eternal Purakh.
0RWM: Nanak says — O mind! Listen, the life-span is going on shortening every day (do not forget the remembrance of the Lord). ||10||
Says Nanak, listen, mind: your life is passing away! ||10||
Says Nanak, hearken, O mortal, your age is diminishing ever.

MXRP: Panch tat = earth, air, water, fire, sky. Ko = of. Chatur = O clever man! Sujan = O wise man!

O Clever and wise man, know that your body is make up of five elements.
O mind, clever and (sujan) knowing, or learned! Know this, that this body the Eternal Purakh has made of the five elements.
D2JK: Jih te = from which elements. Te = from. Tah mah = in those (very elements). Man = accept, know for certain ||11||

Believe it - you shall merge once again into the One, O Nanak, from whom you originated. ||11||
Be you sure, O Nanak, that you shall blend with Him, from whom you have sprung.

38UE: Ghat = the body. Ghat ghat mai = within each and every body. Joo = ji. Pukar = calling out, speaking aloud.

NY49: Bhaunidh = the world-ocean. Utrah = you will cross over ||12||

MFZW: Jih = whose (mind). Parsai = it touches. Abhiman = pride.

Whomsoever touch not pleasure, pain, avarice, worldly love and self-conceit.

2H36: So = that (person). Moorat bhagvan = the very form of God ||13||

- says Nanak, listen, mind: he is the very image of God. ||13||

R074: Ustat = praise. Jih = whose (mind). Kanchan = gold. Loh = iron. Saman = alike.

D6BL: Mukat = release from attachment. Tah = he (has obtained it). Te = you. Jan = understand ||14||

- says Nanak, listen, mind: know that such a person is liberated. ||14||

XP4Z: Mukat = release from the attachment to Maya ||15||

- says Nanak, listen, mind: know that such a person is liberated. ||15||
Says Nanak, hearken you, O my soul, deem you him to be emancipated.

NB48: Bhai = threats (plural of the word 'bhau'). Aan = of others.

O mind, listen! The one who neither gives fear to anyone nor accepts (aan) the fear of another,
5GVA: Giani = the person with an understanding of the spiritual life. Tah = him. Bakhan = call ||16||

- says Nanak, listen, mind: call him spiritually wise. ||16||
Says Nanak, her you, O my soul, call you him, a men of Divine knowledge.

One who has forsaken all sin and corruption, who wears the robes of neutral detachment
He, who has abandoned all sins and has donned the garb of detachedness.

M1K9: Tih nar mathai = upon the forehead of that person ||17||

- says Nanak, listen, mind: good destiny is written on his forehead. ||17||

The mortal, who forsakes ego and realises his Creator-Lord.
O mind! The being who has forsaken the sense of "I" and "mine", and has recognised the Creator Purakh Ram,
Q6YC: Vahu nar = that person. Mukat = saved from the vices. Man = O mind! ||19||

- says Nanak, that person is liberated; O mind, know this as true. ||19||

UMC6: Mamta = the sense of ownership, attachment. Tajai = he forsakes.

2GC1: Tarai = he crosses over. Auran = others. Let udhar = he saves ||22||

LS4E: Rachi = it is made. Meet = O friend! ||25||

so is the universe created; says Nanak, listen, O my friend! ||25||

in the very same way the Creator Purakh has made the creation of the world. ||25||

Says Nanak, without meditating on the Lord, what is the use of this human life? ||30||
Says Nanak, without the Lord's meditation, of what avail is this human life?
The living of such a person, being without the devotion of Hari — Sri Guru ji says: of what use is it? That is, it is in vain. ||30||
392V: Na chetee = na chetai, he does not remember. Mad = in the intoxication. Andh = the person blinded (to the spiritual life).
The person who, blinded (to the spiritual life) by being caught in the attachment to Maya, does not remember the Lord's Name,
The mortal does not think of the Lord; he is blinded by the wine of Maya.
Blinded by the wine of wealth, the mortal remembers not his Lord.
O mind! The one who, through the (mad) pride of Maya, being blind and without knowledge, does not contemplate Ram,
2UU0: Parat = they remain fallen. Tah = upon him. Jam phandh = the nooses of the messengers of death ||31||
Nanak says that without the devotion of the Lord the nooses of the messengers of death remain fallen upon him (around his neck). ||31||
Says Nanak, without meditating on the Lord, he is caught in the noose of Death. ||31||
Says Nanak, without the God's meditation, death's noose falls around him.
Sri Guru ji says: without the devotion of Hari the noose of Yama falls around his neck. ||31||
GP1L: Sangi = a companion, an associate. Sang = with.
(In the world) in comfort many become associates, but in sorrow no one is with you at all.
In good times, there are many companions around, but in bad times, there is no one at all.
Man finds many friends in prosperity, however, none becomes his friend in adversity.
O mind! When beings have comfort, then many (sangi) companions appear; when some misfortune comes, then in that sorrow there is no companion at all.
4GEC: Ant = at the final moment (too). Sahaee = a helper ||32||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on doing the devotion of the Lord; (the Lord) becomes a helper at the final moment (too). ||32||
Says Nanak, vibrate, and meditate on the Lord; He shall be your only Help and Support in the end. ||32||
Says Nanak, O man, ponder you over your God, who shall be your succourer in the end.
Sri Guru ji says: therefore do the devotion of Hari, so that he may be your helper at the end, at the time of death. ||32||
EPRD: Janam janam = in birth after birth. Ko = of. Tras = the fear.
(Forgetting the remembrance of the Lord, the being) goes on wandering through countless births; the fear of the messengers of death does not end (from within it).
Mortals wander lost and confused through countless lifetimes; their fear of death is never removed.
Man wanders about in many births and his fear of death is removed not.
O beloved (mind)! You have wandered through many births, but the fear of Yama has not been wiped away from you.
FGBT: Nirbhai = in the fearless state, in that Lord whom no fear can touch. Pavah = you will obtain ||33||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on doing the devotion of the Lord; (by the grace of devotion) you will obtain a dwelling in that Lord whom no fear can touch. ||33||
Says Nanak, vibrate and meditate on the Lord, and you shall dwell in the Fearless Lord. ||33||
Says Nanak, O man, ponder you over your Lord, that you may abides in the fearless God.
Sri Guru ji says: even now do the devotion of Hari, and you will obtain a dwelling in that fearless place free from the fear of Yama. ||33||
09RX: O Bhagvan! I have made countless (other) efforts; (by those efforts) the pride of the mind is not removed,
I have tried so many things, but the pride of my mind has not been dispelled.
I have grown weary of making many efforts, but my mind's ego is effaced not.
O being! Make your supplication in this way: O Bhagvan! I have made many efforts, but the pride of my mind has not gone.
81YR: Durmat = evil understanding. Siau = with. Phadhio = it remains entangled. Bhagvan = O Bhagvan! ||34||
Nanak's (mind) remains clinging to evil understanding. O Bhagvan! (You yourself) protect it. ||34||
I am engrossed in evil-mindedness, Nanak. O God, please save me! ||34||
I am engrossed in evil-intentions, says Nanak, 'save me, O save me, my illustrious Lord.
Sri Guru ji says: I am caught in such evil understanding; save me from this noose. ||34||
CCE4: Ar = and. Biradh = old age. Phun = (पुनः) again. Teen = three. Jan = know, understand.
Childhood, youth, and then old age — understand (these) three states of life (that come upon a person).
Childhood, youth and old age - know these as the three stages of life.
Know you that there are three stages of life, childhood, youth and then old age.
O mind! The state of childhood, then the state of youth, then the state of old age — know these three states of the body.
KWV5: Nanak says that (but) keep this in mind (that) without the devotion of the Lord all of these go in vain. ||35||
Says Nanak, without meditating on the Lord, everything is useless; you must appreciate this. ||35||
Says Nanak, know you that without the Lord's meditation all are in vain.
Sri Guru ji says: without the devotion of Hari all are in vain. ||35||
4XF6: Karno huto = (whatever) was to be done. Su = that. Kai phandh = in the noose of.
O man grown blind (in the attachment to Maya)! Whatever you had to do, that you did not do; (all your life) you remained caught (only) in the noose of greed.
You have not done what you should have done; you are entangled in the web of greed.
What you should have done, that you have done not. You are entangled in the net of covetousness.
O beloved! What you had to do, that you have not done; you remained caught in the noose of greed.
C987: Samio = the time (of human life). Ram gaio = it has passed away. Andh = O man grown blind (in the attachment to Maya)! ||36||
O Nanak! (All the) time (of life) has passed away (in just this manner). Why do you weep now? (What use is repentance now?) ||36||
Nanak, your time is past and gone; why are you crying now, you blind fool? ||36||
Nanak! When one's times is past, why wail them, O blind man?

Sri Guru ji says: now the time has passed away; O blind one! Why do you weep now? Suffer the fruit of your own doing — the meaning being, he weeps at the moment of death. Then the messengers of Yama say this to him. ||36||
3X2Q: Mai = mah, within. Ram rahio = it is caught. Nahin = not. Meet = O friend!
O friend! The mind that becomes caught in (the attachment to) Maya cannot come out of this attachment (by its own self),
The mind is absorbed in Maya - it cannot escape it, my friend.
O friend, the mind is absorbed in riches and it can escape not from it,
In the same way, O mind! You are revelling in Maya, and you do not come out of Maya.
YQ3X: Moorat = a picture. Chitr = a drawn form. Bheet = a wall ||37||
O Nanak! Just as the drawn form of a picture (upon a wall) does not leave the wall but remains clinging to the wall. ||37||
Nanak, it is like a picture painted on the wall - it cannot leave it. ||37||
just as a picture, painted on the wall, leaves it not, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: as the picture drawn upon a wall does not forsake the wall. ||37||
08CU: Aurai ki aurai = of one thing another.

(Caught in the attachment to Maya) a person goes on asking for something else altogether (instead of the remembrance of the Lord — that is, only for Maya and Maya). (But in the Creator's will) it turns out quite otherwise.
The man wishes for something, but something different happens.
Man seeks something, however, something totally different happens.
A man wishes for something else; O brother! By that reflection something quite other comes about, which is not wished for.
RZPN: Chitvat rahio = you went on thinking. Thagaur = thag-booti, deceptions. Gal = around the neck. Pari = it fell ||38||
O Nanak! (A person) goes on thinking thoughts of cheating (others), (and meanwhile the noose of death) comes and falls around his neck. ||38||
He plots to deceive others, O Nanak, but he places the noose around his own neck instead. ||38||
O Nanak, he thinks of deceiving others, however, a halter is put round his neck.
Sri Guru ji says: his thinking is of deception, that I may cheat others — and the noose of Yama falls around his own neck. ||38||
MDUA: Sukh ke = for the obtaining of worldly comforts. Ko = of. Dukh ko = of sorrows.

(Though the being) goes on making countless efforts for (the obtaining of) comforts, and makes no effort for sorrows (yet even so, according to the will, sorrows do come. Comfort too is obtained only when it is the Lord's will.)
People make all sorts of efforts to find peace and pleasure, but no one tries to earn pain.
Man makes many efforts to obtain peace, however, makes none to fight pain.
O mind, listen! You have made many efforts for the sake of comfort; for sorrow you have made no effort at all.
CBAN: Har bhavai = whatever pleases the Lord ||39||
Nanak says — O mind! Whatever pleases the Lord, that (alone) certainly comes about. ||39||
Says Nanak, listen, mind: whatever pleases God comes to pass. ||39||
Says Nanak, O man, understand, whatever pleases God, that alone happens.
Sri Guru ji says: but whatever pleases Hari, that alone, comfort or sorrow, is obtained. ||39||
NHPV: Bhikhari = a beggar. Sabh ko = of all beings.
The world wanders about (as) a beggar (and does not remember that) the Lord himself is the giver of gifts to all beings.
The world wanders around begging, but the Lord is the Giver of all.
The world wanders about as a beggar and the Lord alone is the Bestower of all.
O mind! The whole world wanders about as a beggar, and the one Ram alone is the giver to all.
ATWR: Man = O mind! Tih = him (the Lord). Hovah = they will become. Kam = all the works ||40||
Nanak says — O mind! Go on remembering that giver Lord, and all your works will keep coming to fulfilment. ||40||
Says Nanak, meditate in remembrance on Him, and all your works will be successful. ||40||
Says Nanak, dwell you on Him, O man, that yours tasks may be fulfilled.
Sri Guru ji says: do the remembrance of him alone, so that your (kam) resolves may be fulfilled. ||40||
R5K9: Jhoothai = of the perishable (world). Kaha kare = why does he do it? Jiau = like. Jan = understand.
(Who knows why a person) goes on taking pride in the perishable world. Understand the world to be (just) like (the things seen in) a dream.
Why do you take such false pride in yourself? You must know that the world is just a dream.
Why take you false pride? Know you that the world is like a dream.
O mind! Know the world to be like a dream; why do you take pride in this false world?
R2PA: In mai = among these (worldly things). Tero = yours (your real companion). Bakhan = having uttered, having explained ||41||
(O brother!) (I) Nanak am telling you rightly that among these (visible things) not one thing at all is your (real companion). ||41||
None of this is yours; Nanak proclaims this truth. ||41||
In it there is nothing, which is yours. Nanak proclaims and narrates this truth.
In this world nothing is yours; Sri Guru ji says: this matter the Vedas and Shastras have all declared and spoken.
NJ31: Garab = (गर्व) pride. Deh ko = of (which) body. Binsai = it is destroyed. Meet = O friend!

O friend! (The) body of which (a person for ever) takes pride (that it is his own — that body) is destroyed in a single instant. (Attachment to other things is far off; even the attachment to this body of one's own is false.)
You are so proud of your body; it shall perish in an instant, my friend.
You entertain pride of your body, which perishes in a moment, O friend.
O friend, mind! The body which you take as your own and over which you take pride, that very body of yours will be destroyed in a single moment.
X9DF: Jih prani = the person who. Jas = praise. Tih = he. Jeet = he has won ||42||
O Nanak! The person who has begun to sing the Lord's praises, he has won the world (its attachment). ||42||
That mortal who chants the Praises of the Lord, O Nanak, conquers the world. ||42||
The mortal, who recites the Lord's praise, he, O Nanak, conquers the whole world.
Sri Guru ji says: the one who has sung the qualities of Hari, he alone has won the world. ||42||
3GKJ: Jih ghat = within whose (person's) heart. Ko = of. Mukta = saved from the vices. Jan = understand.
The person within whose heart the remembrance of the Lord (remains settled) — understand that person to be saved (from the net of attachment).
That person, who meditates in remembrance on the Lord in his heart, is liberated - know this well.
He, within whose mind is the Lord's meditation, consider him to be emancipated.
O mind! The one within whose inner being is the remembrance of the Name of Ram, understand thus, that he is a liberated person.
11UU: Antar = a difference, a distance. Sachi man = accept it as right ||43||
O Nanak! Accept this matter as right, that between that person and the Lord there is no difference. ||43||
There is no difference between that person and the Lord: O Nanak, accept this as the Truth. ||43||
Between that man and God, there is no difference. Accept you this as truth, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: between him and Hari there is no difference at all; understand this saying of mine as true. ||43||
RV93: Kai man = within the mind of. Jih prani kai man = within the mind of which being.
The person within whose mind there is no devotion to the Lord,
That person, who does not feel devotion to God in his mind
The mortal, who enshrines not the devotion of One Lord in his mind,
The being within whose mind there is no devotion to the one Bhagvan,
U4R6: Sookar tan = the body of a pig. Suan tan = the body of a dog. Tah = of that (person) ||44||
O Nanak! Understand his body to be just like the body of (some) pig or the body of (some) dog. ||44||
- O Nanak, know that his body is like that of a pig, or a dog. ||44||
O Nanak, deem you his body to be like that of a hog and a dog.
Sri Guru ji says: understand his body to be just as the pig and the dog are. ||44||
VH7H: Ko = of. Grih = the house. Tajat nahi = he does not leave it.
As a dog for ever (keeps hold of) the house (the door of the house) of (its) master and never leaves it at all,
A dog never abandons the home of his master.
As a dog never abandons the home of his Master of his Master for aye;
The dog, as he does not forsake the house of the master who gives him his food,
UT9M: Ih bidh = in this manner. Bhajau = go on doing devotion. Ik man hue = with the mind made one. Ik chit hue = with the thought made one ||45||
O Nanak! In this very manner, with the mind made one and the thought made one, go on doing the devotion of the Lord (so that his door may never be left at all). ||45||
O Nanak, in just the same way, vibrate, and meditate on the Lord, single-mindedly, with one-pointed consciousness. ||45||
Nanak, in this way, you contemplate on God with focused mind and whole heart.
Sri Guru ji says: in this manner do the devotion of Hari with one mind and one thought, becoming firm. ||45||
5FBT: Ar = and. Kar = having done. Man mai = within the mind. Guman = pride.
(Forsaking the devotion of the Lord, a person) bathes at places of pilgrimage, keeps fasts, gives in charity, and then takes pride within (his own) mind (that he has become religious)
Those who make pilgrimages to sacred shrines, observe ritualistic fasts and make donations to charity while still taking pride in their minds
Whosoever, while going on pilgrimage, fasting and giving alms, takes pride in his mind,
The one who, having done fasts, pilgrimages and charity, then takes pride in these, that I have done them —
P9CD: Tih = his (these pilgrimages, fasts and charity). Nihfal = in vain. Kunchar = of an elephant ||46||
(But) O Nanak! All these deeds of his (go) in vain (just) as the bathing (done) by an elephant. (Note: after bathing, an elephant throws ash and dust over itself) ||46||
- O Nanak, their actions are useless, like the elephant, who takes a bath, and then rolls in the dust. ||46||
Nanak, these deeds of him go in vain like the bathing of an elephant.

Sri Guru ji says: the pilgrimages, fasts and the rest of that proud person become as fruitless as the bathing of (kunchar) an elephant is fruitless. For by bathing the dirt is washed away, and then the elephant, coming out, puts dust upon its own head with its own trunk; in the very same way the being, through pride, destroys the fruit of pilgrimages and the rest. ||46||
NH6N: Kampio = it is trembling. Pag = the feet. Dagmage = they are faltering. Te = from. Nain = the eyes. Jot = the light.
(When old age has come, a person's) head begins to tremble, (as he walks) his feet falter, the light of the eyes is destroyed,
The head shakes, the feet stagger, and the eyes become dull and weak.
The head shakes, the feet stagger and the eyes become devoid of luster,
The head too has begun to tremble, the feet too have begun (dagmagai) to waver and do not fall straight, and the eyes too have become without (jot) light.
PGFM: Ih bidh = this condition. Tau = even then. Leen = absorbed. Har ras leen = absorbed in the savour of the Lord's Name ||47||
Nanak says — this condition (of the body) comes about with old age, and even then (the attachment to Maya is so strong that a person) is not absorbed in the savour of the Lord's Name. ||47||
Says Nanak, this is your condition. And even now, you have not savored the sublime essence of the Lord. ||47||
this has become your condition, O man, even then you are absorbed not in the Lord's Name Nectar, Says Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: this has become the state of these beings, and even then they do not become (leen) intent upon the savour of Hari. ||47||

UEBN: Nij kar = taking it as one's own. Ko = any being. Kahoo ko = of anyone at all.
I have gone on looking at the world (up to now) taking it as my own, (but here) no one belongs to anyone at all (as their own for ever).
I had looked upon the world as my own, but no one belongs to anyone else.
I have looked upon everyone as my own, however, I have observed that, in this world, no one is another's friend.
I have looked at the world (nij kar) making it my own; in this world no one belongs to anyone.
7YTR: O Nanak! What is ever-abiding is (only) the devotion of the Lord. Keep this (devotion) threaded within (your own) mind. ||48||
O Nanak, only devotional worship of the Lord is permanent; enshrine this in your mind. ||48||
Nanak, permanent is only the devotional service of God. Enshrine you that in your mind.
Sri Guru ji says: the one devotion of Hari is abiding; keep that alone within the mind. ||48||
BS92: O friend! Know this matter for truth, that the whole creation of the world is perishable.
The world and its affairs are totally false; know this well, my friend.
Totally false is the structure of the world. Know you this, O my friend.
O friend! However much creation of the world there is, all of it is false; understand this.
CHVQ: Kah = kahai, he says. Baloo = sand. Bheet = a wall ||49||
Nanak says that, like a wall of sand, no thing at all (in the world) is ever-abiding. ||49||
Says Nanak, it is like a wall of sand; it shall not endure. ||49||
Says Nanak, like the wall of sand, it remains not permanent.
Sri Guru ji says: as a wall of sand does not remain standing, in this same way the creation of the world too is destructible in a moment. ||49||
2G6B: Gaio = he has gone, he has departed. Ja kau = the one (Ravan) who. Bahu parvar = (is said to be) one of a great family.
(Look! Sri) Ram (Chandra) departed, Ravan too passed away, who is said to have been one of a great family.
Raam Chand passed away, as did Raawan, even though he had lots of relatives.
Ram Chander passed away and Rawan, too, who has a large family, had to pass away.

These three saloks were written to Mata ji: See, Sri Ram Chandra was an incarnation, and even he did not keep his body in this world but carried it to the next. That Ravan who had a hundred thousand sons and a hundred and twenty-five thousand grandsons, and beyond them their wives and sons, his own wives, and all their relations — he had a great family, and he too departed from the world.
MSFT: Nanak says — (here) there is no thing at all that abides for ever. (This) world is (just) like a dream. ||50||
Says Nanak, nothing lasts forever; the world is like a dream. ||50||
Says Nanak, nothing is ever-lasting, the world is like a dream.
Sri Guru ji says: in this false creation of the world nothing at all is abiding; this world is like a dream. ||50||
KYJQ: Ta ki = of that (matter). Keejeeai = one ought to do. Anhoni = that which does not happen, the impossible.
(As for death and the like,) one ought to worry over that (event) which is never going to happen at all.
People become anxious, when something unexpected happens.
Only then one should worry, if a thing, not expected to happen, comes to pass.
Worry ought to be done over that thing which would be some unheard-of and astonishing happening.
FKND: Ko = of. Marag = the road. Sansar ko marag = the road of the world ||51||
O Nanak! The very way of the world is this, that (here) no being at all is ever-abiding. ||51||
This is the way of the world, O Nanak; nothing is stable or permanent. ||51||
This is the way of the world. None is ever stable, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: the forsaking of the body — this is the road of the whole world, and therefore in this world no one is abiding. ||51||
7C65: Binas hai = it will be destroyed. Paro = one who is to perish. Kai = or. Kal = tomorrow.
(In the world) whoever has been born will (certainly) be destroyed; (everyone) is to depart from here today or tomorrow.
Whatever has been created shall be destroyed; everyone shall perish, today or tomorrow.
Whosoever is born, he must perish. Every one shall fall today or tomorrow.
Whatever has come into being, all of it will be destroyed — whether it perish today, or perish tomorrow, or (paro) perish the day after.
AAV4: Chhad = having forsaken. Janjal = the nooses of the attachment to Maya ||52||
O Nanak! (Therefore) cast off all the nooses (of the attachment to Maya) and go on singing the qualities of the Lord. ||52||
O Nanak, sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord, and give up all other entanglements. ||52||
Nanak, you sing the Lord's praises and lay aside all other entanglements.
Sri Guru ji says: therefore forsake these entanglements and sing the qualities of Hari. ||52|| ☬ 1. A salok written for the testing of Sri Guru Gobind Singh ji:
31ZA: Bal = (spiritual) strength. Bandhan = the nooses (of the attachment to Maya). Pare = they have fallen, they fall. Upae = a means.

(Parted from the Lord's Name, when the nooses of the attachment to Maya) come and fall (upon a person, then for the cutting of those nooses the spiritual) strength within a person is exhausted (and no means at all can be made by a person to withstand Maya).
My strength is exhausted, and I am in bondage; I cannot do anything at all.
My strength is exhausted, I am in chains and I can make not any effort.
All our strength has gone, and bonds have fallen upon the body; now it is the final hour, and no effort of our own avails.
PG76: Ab = now, at that moment. Ot = the support. Har = O Lord! Sahae = a helper ||53||

Nanak says — O Lord! At such a moment (now) your support alone remains. As you became the helper of the elephant (to save it from the crocodile), so become my helper. (The meaning being, to obtain release from the bonds of attachment to Maya, supplication at the Lord's door is the one and only means.) ||53||
Says Nanak, now, the Lord is my Support; He will help me, as He did the elephant. ||53||
Say Nanak, God alone is now my refuge. He will help me as he did the elephant.
Sri Guru ji says: now in every way your support alone is mine. As you, being Hari, protected the elephant, in that same way give help to me also. ||53||
V024: Chhute = they are broken. Sabh kichh upae = every effort.

(When a person falls at the Lord's door, then within him spiritual) strength arises to withstand Maya, the bonds (of the attachment to Maya) are broken, and every means (of withstanding attachment) can succeed.
My strength has been restored, and my bonds have been broken; now, I can do everything.
I have regained my Power, my bonds are broken and all options are open on to me.

Reading this salok of testing, Sri Kalgidhar ji wrote a reply in one salok from Sri Anandpur ji. In Bhai Banno's recension "Mahalla 10" is also written. O Satguru, cause of all causes! That which is named strength has arisen from you yourself; and all bonds are broken by you; and every effort can succeed only when done by you.
6HHQ: Hot = it can be. Sabh kichh = every thing ||54||
So, Nanak says — (O Lord!) Everything is in your hand (the Maya you created is also under your own control; to be saved from it) you alone can be the helper. ||54||
Nanak: everything is in Your hands, Lord; You are my Helper and Support. ||54||
Nanak, everything is in yours hands. It is only you who can assist yourself.

Sri Guru ji says: O form of Guru Nanak Dev! Everything is in your own hand, and you alone become the helper of all the devotees. ||54|| ☬ Taking this very reply, the Sikh who came to Delhi — by his own hand were sent the offering for the seat and three saloks in the manner of a robe of honour. In the first the state of the world is written, in the second the certainty, in the third the teaching.
01LW: Sang = a companion. Sabh = all. Taj gae = they left, they leave. Sath = with.
(When at the final moment) all the companions and friends leave, when no one at all can keep company,
My associates and companions have all deserted me; no one remains with me.
My associates and mates have all left me. None has remained with me to the last.
O Raghunath, Eternal Purakh! The meaning being, we too are in this same lineage. So now the companions and friends have all forsaken us, and not one has kept company with us.
60ZF: Ih bipat mai = in this misfortune, in this loneliness. Raghunath tek = the support of the Lord ||55||
Nanak says — even at that moment of (the) misfortune (of loneliness) it is the Lord's support alone that remains. (So, go on remembering the Lord's Name for ever.) ||55||
Says Nanak, in this tragedy, the Lord alone is my Support. ||55||
Says Nanak, in this calamity, the Lord alone is my support.
Sri Guru ji says: at the time of such misfortune your support alone is mine. ||55|| ☬ At that time, seeing the Creator Purakh face to face, and seeing Bhai Gurdita ji, this word was spoken.
L63U: Rahio = it remains, it stays a companion. Sadhoo = the Guru. Gur gobind = the Eternal Being.
(Even at the final moment the Lord's) Name remains (with the being), the Guru (in the form of the bani) remains with him, the Eternal Being is with him,
The Naam remains; the Holy Saints remain; the Guru, the Lord of the Universe, remains.
Only the Lord is eternal, His Name remains eternal and so are the saints.
First, the Name has stayed with us; and second, the Sadhu Bhai Gurdita has stayed with us; and third, Guru Gobind — that is, Parmesvar who is worthy of worship — has stayed with us.
52FC: Kin = whoever. Gurmant = the Guru's teaching (of remembering the Lord's Name) ||56||

Nanak says — in this world, whichever person has settled the Guru's teaching (of remembering the Lord's Name) within himself for ever (and has repeated the Name, for him these become helpers at the final moment). ||56||
Says Nanak, how rare are those who chant the Guru's Mantra in this world. ||56||
Says Nanak, rare is the one, who reflects over the Guru's word, in this world.
Sri Guru ji says: in this world (kin) some rare one has taken the Guru's teaching and repeated the Name. ||56|| ☬ Bringing it to a close, he makes his supplication:
1RTH: Ur = the heart. Ur mah = within the heart. Gahio = he has grasped it, he has settled it firmly. Ja kai sam = equal to which (Lord's Name).
O Lord! The person who has settled within his heart that Name of yours, equal to which there is no other,
I have enshrined the Lord's Name within my heart; there is nothing equal to it.
The Lord's Name, of which there is no peer, I have clasped to my mind.
O Ram! I have borne your Name within my heart, equal to which Name there is no other thing at all.
ATZ1: Jih simrat = by remembering which Name of the Lord. Sankat = sorrow and affliction ||57||1||
and by remembering which every sorrow and affliction is removed — to that person your vision too comes about. ||57||1||
Meditating in remembrance on it, my troubles are taken away; I have received the Blessed Vision of Your Darshan. ||57||1||
Such is your Name, O Lord, remembering which my troubles end and I am blessed wit Yours vision.
By the mere remembrance of which all kinds of affliction are wiped away, and (tuharo) your vision is obtained. ||57||
PGA7: Mundavani = (mud = to please, to gladden; modayati = pleases). Mudavani, or mundavani = the thing that gives spiritual delight.

(Mundavani) They speak of the cover: as, having placed the prasad in a thal, they then cover it over from above with a cover. So by means of this Mundavani a rule was made for the future, that no other bani should be added. The place for the bani of Sri Guru Teg Bahadur Sahib Ji had been left aside from the very beginning.
WB4V: Thal vichi = in (that heart-) thal. Tinni vastu = three things (satu, santokhu and vichar).
In (that man's heart-) thal three things remain settled — high conduct, contentment and the understanding of spiritual life,
Upon this Plate, three things have been placed: Truth, Contentment and Contemplation.
In the platter are placed three things, truth, contentment and meditations.
In the thal which is Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji three things have been placed: the speaking of truth, contentment as things come, and this thing — reflect, that is to say, understand.
YK5U: Amrit = that which gives spiritual life. Jis ka = (because of the postposition 'ka' the aunkar of the word 'jisu' has dropped) of which (Nam). Sabhsu = to every being. Adharo = support.
(in whose heart-thal) the Nam of Parmatma that gives spiritual life comes to dwell (this 'amrit nam' is such) that its support is (necessary) for every being.
The Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam, the Name of our Lord and Master, has been placed upon it as well; it is the Support of all.
The Nectar-Name of the Lord, who is the support of all, has also been put therein.

The third is the Nam of Parmesar, of the form of amrit, which the Gurus have placed there; of which Nam every single one has the support — that is to say, whoever repeats it, high or low, it liberates them all.
17SA: Ko = any (man). Bhunchai = he partakes, he eats, he enjoys. Tis ka = (because of the postposition 'ka' the aunkar of the word 'tisu' has dropped) of that (man). Udharo = deliverance, rescue from the vices.
(This spiritual food) if any man goes on eating always, then that man's rescue from the vices comes about.
One who eats it and enjoys it shall be saved.
If some one partakes this and relishes it, he is emancipated.

Whoever eats this food, or (bhunche) feeds it to others; or, those who eat it now and those who will eat it hereafter — of each such one the deliverance comes about and will come about, of him who has made this food.
64UY: Eh vastu = this thing that gives spiritual delight, this mudavani. Taji nah jai = cannot be renounced. Rakhu = keep it safe. Uri = in the heart. Dharo = settle it.
(If spiritual deliverance is needed, then) this Nam-thing that gives spiritual delight cannot be renounced; keep it always safe within your own heart.
This thing can never be forsaken; keep this always and forever in your mind.
This can be forsaken not, so ever and always keep you this enshrined in your mind.
He to whom the taste of this relish has come — by him this thing cannot then be renounced; therefore keep it settled in the heart day after day.
U5NP: Tam = (tamas) darkness. Tam sansaru = the world made pitch-dark (by reason of the vices). Lagi = having fallen. Sabhu = everywhere. Brahm pasaro = the expanse of Parmatma, the manifestation of Parmatma's own self ||1||
O Nanak! (By the grace of this Nam-thing) by falling at Prabhu's feet the pitch-dark world-ocean can be crossed, and everywhere the manifestation of Parmatma's own self (begins to be seen). ||1||
The dark world-ocean is crossed over, by grasping the Feet of the Lord; O Nanak, it is all the extension of God. ||1||
Repairing to the Lord's feet, the dark world ocean is crossed; O Nanak, everything is an extension of the Lord.

The fruit of it is this: that world which is of the form of (tam) darkness — from that one is ferried across by falling at the feet of the Gurus. Sri Guru Ji says: all is the expanse of Brahm alone; O brother! Upon reflecting truly, this becomes evident.
DH2P: Salok of Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji makes supplication at the completion of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji:
Z51B: Kita = the kindness done. Jato nahi = I have not understood the worth (of the kindness You did). Maino = to me. Kitoi = You have made (me). Jogu = fit, a fitting (vessel, to hold the gift of the kindness). Mai
(O Prabhu!) I cannot understand the worth of the kindness You have done; (to hold the gift of that kindness) You Yourself have made me a fitting vessel.
I have not appreciated what You have done for me, Lord; only You can make me worthy.
O Lord, I have not appreciated, what you have done for me, you have made me worthy of Your service.
O Akal Purakh! I have understood nothing of the kindness You have done; (i) assuredly, of all these matters — and You have made me (jogu) fit, that is to say capable in every matter.
N41C: Nirguniare = in me, devoid of virtue. Ko gunu = any virtue. Ape = Himself.
In me, devoid of virtue, there is no virtue at all. You Yourself came to feel pity for me.
I am unworthy - I have no worth or virtues at all. You have taken pity on me.
In me, the meritless one, there is no virtue. You of Yourself, O my Lord, have taken pity on me.
In me, devoid of virtue, there was not any virtue at all; pity for me (paioi) came to You of Yourself.
ZCJH: O Prabhu! Pity for me arose in Your mind, Your mercy came upon me, and then I found the friend Guru. (This kindness of Yours cannot be forgotten.)
You took pity on me, and blessed me with Your Mercy, and I have met the True Guru, my Friend.
You have shown mercy and rained Yours benediction on me. I have now met with the True Guru, my friend.

When the pity came, then (miharamati) exceeding grace came about, and He completed the four means. When all the means were obtained, then Sri Satigur, the friend and the unfeigned benefactor, came to be met.
VC9N: Milai = comes. Tan = then. Jivan = I come to life, spiritual life is found by me. Thivai = becomes. Haria = green with spiritual life ||1||
Nanak says — (now, from the beloved Guru) when (Your) Nam comes to me, then spiritual life arises within me; my body and my mind come into blossom (by the grace of that spiritual life). ||1||
O Nanak, if I am blessed with the Naam, I live, and my body and mind blossom forth. ||1||
Nanak! Then alone I live and my body and soul blossom forth, if I am blessed with the Lord's Name.

Sri Guru Ji says: when by the grace of the Satigurus Your Nam comes to me, I live. As in: ☬ 'Akha jiva visarai mari jau.' ☬ And again: ☬ 'Marnan bisarnan gobindah jivnan nam dhivnah.' ☬ By that my mind, the subtle antahkaran, and my body, the gross frame, all are turning green. So the opening is from Satinam and the conclusion is Satinam — if the Nam is obtained, then I live. ||1||
